title: cursor-agent rounds run inside the macOS round sandbox: the adapter hands cursor a short private per-round CURSOR_DATA_DIR it may write, so cursor no longer falls back to the denied /tmp/.cursor, and a codex usage-limit message counts its vendor unavailable so the fallback chain moves on
acceptance: Why. cursor-agent rounds cannot run inside the macOS round sandbox today. Evidence: worker round state/runs/worker-imani-t215-r2b/cursor-agent-t3ny69sr (2026-10-05) exited 1 after 6 s with `Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, mkdir '/tmp/.cursor/Users-benjamin-Desktop-firstmate-workflow-state-worktrees-T-215'`. Reproduced by firstmate on 2026-10-05 on macOS Darwin 24.6.0 with cursor-agent 2026.10.01-e373342: `bin/fm-sandbox.sh run --policy=<worker policy> --root=<scratch worktree> --tmp=<round tmp, 198 characters> --vendor=cursor-agent -- cursor-agent -p --trust --sandbox disabled -f --mode ask --output-format text 'Reply with exactly: OK'` with `AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE=memory` and the crew key -> exit 1, `Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, mkdir '/tmp/.cursor/private-tmp-…-0d8178c'`. No task prompt was used; the key was never printed.

Mechanism (root cause). cursor-agent's bundle (`index.js`) picks its per-project data directory as: base = `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` or `$HOME/.cursor`; candidate = `<base>/projects`; if the candidate is longer than 84 characters it tries `<base>` itself, and if that is also longer than 84 it falls back to the hard-coded `/tmp/.cursor` (the function `d(t){let e=u(); e.length>84&&(e=c(), e.length>84&&(e="/tmp/.cursor")); …}`; a final path over 92 characters is cut to 84 plus a 7-character sha256 suffix). The round sandbox gives every round `HOME=$tmp/home` under the round's own temp directory (bin/fm-sandbox.sh:634-638, design §13.2 'A normal environment inside every round'), and that temp directory (`mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-round.XXXXXX"`, bin/adapters/_lib.sh:424, under the operator's long macOS `$TMPDIR`) makes `$HOME/.cursor/projects` far longer than 84 characters, so cursor always falls back to `/tmp/.cursor`, which is not a write root of the round (correctly), and the mkdir is denied. `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` is read by the same bundle and is not in `--help`.

Change 1, the adapter (the fix). bin/adapters/cursor-agent.sh, after `fm_adapter_policy` (:109) and before `fm_adapter_confine` (:123): make a private short directory `cursor_data="$(mktemp -d /tmp/fmc.XXXXXX)"` - an explicit `/tmp`, never `$TMPDIR`, which by then is the long round temp (_lib.sh:438) - resolve it with `pwd -P` only if the result still keeps `$cursor_data/projects` at or under 84 characters (on macOS `/tmp` resolves to `/private/tmp`, 32 characters in all, which fits; if it ever did not fit, the adapter prints `cursor-agent: cannot make a short data directory for cursor; refusing the round` to stderr and exits 70); on mktemp failure the same message and exit 70. It is mode 0700 and owned by the operator, created by the unconfined adapter, outside the sandbox. Export `CURSOR_DATA_DIR="$cursor_data"` (a fixed value; an inherited operator environment value is overwritten; FM_ADAPTER_ARGS is argv, not an environment-setting interface, and cannot override this fixed export). Then, after `fm_adapter_confine` returns, when FM_LAUNCH is the OS sandbox (`${FM_LAUNCH[1]}` = `run`), insert `--write=$cursor_data` before FM_LAUNCH's trailing `--` (the same kind of extra write root `fm_adapter_confine` already adds for `FM_ATTEMPT_DIR`, _lib.sh:493-496). In `plain` mode (the operator's FM_CREW_UNSANDBOXED hatch) the variable is still exported and no `--write` is added. Nothing else is granted: `/tmp` as a whole stays outside every round (the control recorded below proves a `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` that is not a write root is still denied). A comment beside the code says why: the 84-character fallback to `/tmp/.cursor`, the long round HOME, and that the directory is per round so no two rounds share cursor's project state.

Change 1, cleanup. The directory is removed on every exit path of the adapter after it is made: immediately after mktemp succeeds, before pwd -P or the length check, the adapter re-sets the EXIT trap that fm_adapter_policy installed (_lib.sh:433, `rm -rf '$FM_ROUND_TMP' '$FM_ROUND_CTL'`) to remove all three paths (`'$FM_ROUND_TMP' '$FM_ROUND_CTL' '$cursor_data'`), so the existing INT/TERM/HUP traps (_lib.sh:435-437, which turn a signal into an EXIT path) clean it up too; the round temp and control directories are still removed exactly as before. The model check (`fm_adapter_model_listcheck … cursor-agent --list-models`, :102-107) runs before the directory exists, unconfined, with the operator's own short HOME, and is unchanged.

Verified fix. Recorded by firstmate on 2026-10-05, same host, same round temp (198 characters), same argv as the failing reproduction: `C=$(mktemp -d /tmp/fmc.XXXXXX)` (`/tmp/fmc.lA7BLL`), `AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE=memory CURSOR_DATA_DIR=$C bin/fm-sandbox.sh run … --write=$C --vendor=cursor-agent -- cursor-agent -p --trust --sandbox disabled -f --mode ask --output-format text 'Reply with exactly: OK'` -> exit 0, output `OK`, cursor created `$C/projects/…`, no keychain warning; `$C` was then removed. Control: `CURSOR_DATA_DIR=/tmp/fmc.nowrite` without `--write` -> exit 1, `Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, mkdir '/tmp/fmc.nowrite/projects/…'`, so the sandbox still confines everything it was not explicitly given.

Change 2, codex's usage limit is an unavailable vendor. Evidence: codex round state/runs/worker-imani-t215-r2/codex-nhgqxqrj (2026-10-05) printed exactly these two JSONL events and exited 1: `{"type":"error","message":"You’ve hit your usage limit. Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage to purchase more credits or try again at Oct 10th, 2026 7:58 AM."}` and `{"type":"turn.failed","error":{"message":"You’ve hit your usage limit. Visit https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage to purchase more credits or try again at Oct 10th, 2026 7:58 AM."}}` (the apostrophe is U+2019). `fm_adapter_codex_verdict` (bin/adapters/_lib.sh:626-667) matches `_FM_SIG` (:44) against error and turn.failed diagnostics, but `_FM_SIG` has no usage-limit phrase, so the verdict was 1 (unfit) instead of 2, and `fm_run_chain` (bin/fm-config.sh, moves on only when rc is 2) never tried the next vendor. Fix: add the alternative `hit your usage limit` to `_FM_SIG`. Chosen without the apostrophe on purpose: the codex verdict matches `json.dumps(...)` of the diagnostic, which escapes U+2019 as `\u2019`, and a bash grep under the C locale sees it as three bytes; `hit your usage limit` matches in all of them. The same alternative is added to fm-auth-probe.sh's `_FM_QUOTA` (:290), which mirrors `_FM_SIG`'s quota phrases. Managed Codex (FM_ATTEMPT_DIR set) model/tool payload remains non-diagnostic: only error and turn.failed diagnostics classify availability. The legacy transcript path (non-Codex vendors and Codex without FM_ATTEMPT_DIR) still scans the whole transcript, so the same phrase quoted in that path yields rc 2; this task does not redesign that legacy behavior.

Fixtures and stubs answer like the vendor. Every new test that simulates the codex usage limit uses the captured event bytes verbatim, including U+2019, for ensure_ascii=False and legacy-text cases; ensure_ascii=True fixtures reserialize the same JSON objects, escaping U+2019, without paraphrasing their messages; the cursor-agent fallback is simulated by a stub that computes its data directory the way the bundle does (`${CURSOR_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.cursor}/projects`, the 84-character rule, then `/tmp/.cursor`) and fails with cursor's own text `Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, mkdir '<dir>'` and exit 1 when that directory is not writable to it. Because fake sandbox-exec/bwrap enforce no write boundary themselves, the Cursor stub decides writability from recorded profile.sb or bwrap.args roots, as writable_in in adapter-policy does. It never writes outside those roots, including /tmp/.cursor.

Tests (fail-first; workers do not run suites, CI and the gates verify). tests/adapter-policy.test.sh: `round_locations` (:125-134) gains `cursor-agent) printf '%s\n' CURSOR_DATA_DIR ;;` (replacing the comment that cursor is handed no location of its own), so the existing loop asserts the round is handed `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` and may write it, on darwin and linux; the 'cursor-agent is handed no XDG_CONFIG_HOME of fm's' assertion (:171-174) stays unchanged as a regression guard. tests/adapter-protocol.test.sh (or the suite already holding the cursor-agent adapter stub): one round with a long caller TMPDIR records the stub's `CURSOR_DATA_DIR`, asserts it is under `/tmp/fmc.` or `/private/tmp/fmc.`, `<it>/projects` is at most 84 characters, FM_LAUNCH carried `--write=<it>`, and after the adapter returns the directory no longer exists; a second case where the stub exits 1 also leaves no directory. tests/codex-availability.test.sh `test_real_errors_and_cli_failures` (:138-149): the two recorded lines, each alone and together, after `self.stream()`, written with `ensure_ascii` true and false, with rc 1 -> 2. tests/adapter-verdict.test.sh: append the recorded message to broken_lines so both the rc 2 loop and _FM_SIG alternative completeness check cover it. Healthy lines remain rc 0 regression guards. tests/config.test.sh's existing FM_EXIT_codex=2 chain case (:624) remains a regression guard: rc 2 advances to the next vendor (claude). Do not add a stub adapter that prints usage-limit text and exits 1: fm_run_chain consumes only the exit code. The new real-adapter cases in tests/codex-availability.test.sh prove usage-limit text maps rc 1 to 2. tests/auth-probe.test.sh: add a codex status reply with the recorded usage-limit text that yields quota-exhausted, using only the codex status case (:425-428); the Cursor quota-pair loop (:242-245) is unchanged. Each assertion of new behaviour is red on main 51ee2e8; the XDG_CONFIG_HOME guard and the existing quota cases pass on main by design and say so in a comment. Additional new Cursor assertions in the adapter protocol/policy fixtures: failing mktemp and an overlong resolved path both return 70 with the exact fixed refusal message; successful allocation records mode 0700 and owner equal to the invoking operator; an inherited CURSOR_DATA_DIR is replaced; post-allocation confine refusal exits 2 and removes the recorded cursor directory, round temp and control directories; TERM after allocation exercises the existing signal-to-EXIT path and removes all three recorded paths. Record actual paths before triggering failure/signals, wait for adapter completion and never assert cleanup against an unset variable. Extend tests/adapter-login.test.sh hatch loop (:295-306) for Cursor plain mode: its stub receives the fresh CURSOR_DATA_DIR but no --write argument. Managed Codex model and tool payload containing the exact recorded usage-limit message still return 0; legacy transcript classification of that quoted phrase returns 2 as new fail-first behavior (the legacy scan mechanism remains unchanged). The new allocation/plain-mode cases are red on base; the exact legacy usage-limit message classification is new fail-first behavior; unchanged round/control cleanup, legacy whole-transcript scanning mechanics and existing quota cases are guards, explicitly labeled.

Callers, mirrors and fixtures checked (grep `CURSOR_DATA_DIR`, `/tmp/.cursor`, `_FM_SIG`, `_FM_QUOTA`, `usage limit` and `cursor-agent` over bin/, tests/, design/ and skills/): bin/adapters/cursor-agent.sh, bin/adapters/_lib.sh (`_FM_SIG` only) and bin/fm-auth-probe.sh (`_FM_QUOTA` only) change. Read through unchanged paths and not changed: bin/fm-sandbox.sh (its scrub does not name `CURSOR_DATA_DIR`, so the variable reaches the confined CLI; `--write` already exists), bin/lib/fm_registry.py, bin/fm-config.sh (`fm_run_chain`), bin/fm-worker.sh, bin/fm-review.sh, bin/fm-canary.sh. bin/fm-doctor.sh's quota fix line (:505-514) matches `[Qq]uota`/`[Rr]ate*imit`/`429` and `fm_auth_quota_reset` (_lib.sh:295-302) knows `try again in` but not `try again at`, so a codex usage-limit canary row is not summarised as quota; that is a follow-up, not this task. Stubs that answer cursor-agent without looking at `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` keep passing unchanged: tests/worker-auth.test.sh, tests/canary.test.sh, tests/adapter-protocol.test.sh's existing cursor stubs, tests/lib/herdr.py. bin/adapters/_contract.md gets one sentence where it lists what a cursor round is handed. No test outside those named needs a change; if one does, it is a scope miss to report.

Design (edit in place, no tail section, T-189). Home §13.2, 'A normal environment inside every round' (base 51ee2e8, design.md:4523): after the XDG_CONFIG_HOME exception (:4537-4550), document Cursor's private short CURSOR_DATA_DIR, its 84-character reason, per-round 0700 /tmp/fmc.XXXXXX directory, --write grant only in run mode, exit cleanup and continued denial of /tmp itself. Amend §13.1's cursor-agent login and flag rows (:4070, :4254) to mention the data directory. In §13.3 near :4766, document Codex's recorded usage-limit diagnostic as an unavailable vendor (exit 2) so the existing chain moves on.

In flight and eligibility. Existing rounds keep their frozen code snapshots and need no restart. No stored record or pin format changes. Dispatches from pre-existing sessions/autopilots retain their old frozen FM_CODE_ROOT and old adapter behavior until a new session snapshots the updated code; retained snapshots are never rewritten. Newly dispatched rounds using that updated snapshot get the Cursor directory and the Codex classification fix. Add a focused frozen-old/new snapshot regression in tests/adapter-protocol.test.sh using disposable copied code roots and the same vendor stub: the retained old snapshot stays byte-identical and retains old behavior, while a newly copied updated snapshot exports the short directory and classifies the recorded Codex refusal as rc 2. Keep old-snapshot expectations explicitly labeled guards; the new-snapshot behavior is fail-first. Launch eligibility comes from a fresh auth probe; the historical quota reset date is not current availability evidence. No config.yaml change. Other vendors' data directories are unchanged.

Out of scope: widening the round sandbox to `/tmp` or to `/tmp/.cursor`, any bin/fm-sandbox.sh change, shortening the round temp path, the keychain deny and `AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE` (T-197), the doctor's quota summary and `try again at` reset phrase (follow-up), other vendors' data directories.
